validity.recommendation: none -- existence, classification and current ownership resolved, keep row as recorded (except the StartYear1 correction filed separately below)
validity.researcher_notes: SYSTEM-LEVEL FACTS (per orchestrator dispatch, established here as the cluster anchor): Great Basin Gas Transmission Company ('Great Basin'), formerly known as Paiute Pipeline Company, is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Southwest Gas Corporation ('Southwest Gas'), which is in turn a wholly-owned subsidiary of the publicly traded Southwest Gas Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: SWX, CIK 0001692115) -- confirmed by Great Basin's own official site (greatbasingtc.com: 'Great Basin Gas Transmission Company (Great Basin), formerly known as Paiute Pipeline Company, is a wholly owned subsidiary of Southwest Gas Corporation') and independently by Southwest Gas Holdings' FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-02-25, accession 0001692115-26-000062), which describes Great Basin as a FERC-regulated interstate natural gas pipeline subsidiary serving two local distribution companies (NV Energy and Southwest Gas itself) in northern Nevada. Great Basin's own site states the Main Line 'extends from the Idaho-Nevada border to the Nevada-California border' -- consistent with the digitized route geometry (../GOIT-GGIT-pipeline-routes/data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P7856.geojson, 15 LineString features, combined extent lon -120.026 to -115.785 / lat 38.856 to 41.998, i.e. Idaho border to the Reno/south-Tahoe area) and with EIA's Aug-2026 Natural Gas Pipeline Projects release (sheet 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects', Excel row 57), whose notes field independently describes 'Great Basin Gas Transmission's existing 898-mile transmission system (formerly Paiute Pipeline, subsidiary of Southwest Gas), which stretches from the Idaho-Nevada border across northern Nevada to Reno-Sparks/Carson City and Lake Tahoe.' EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE: this is a real, currently operating FERC-jurisdictional interstate transmission system, correctly classified, and no other row in the 42-row roster describes this same Main Line (the four sibling rows P7857-P7860 are separate, later expansion/lateral/replacement projects on the same system, not duplicates of this trunk). Downstream/upstream interconnects: Great Basin's Idaho-border receipt point interconnects with Northwest Pipeline (and, per industry references, indirectly with other interstate systems feeding that corridor); the roster's description of Ruby Pipeline and Paiute-lateral interconnects further south in Nevada was not independently re-verified in this pass (out of scope for the Main Line's own 15 worklist units) but is consistent with the route geometry's path through northern/central Nevada. CAVEAT: one route-geometry feature (fid=8) appears to nudge slightly into California near South Lake Tahoe; this is a minor, inconclusive geometry observation (not corroborated against a sourced California terminus) and is not elevated to a full attribution concern given the operator's own explicit 'Nevada-California border' phrasing for the system's edge, not a stated crossing into California proper.

validity.recommendation: correct StartYear1 from 1988 to 1963 -- 1988 appears to be the year the pipeline's operating subsidiary was reorganized/renamed 'Paiute Pipeline Company', not the physical pipeline's original construction/in-service year
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's recorded StartYear1=1988 traces to a PHMSA-hosted public-awareness flyer (pipelinesafetyinfo.com/user/file/Nevada/Great Basin Gas Transmission Company.pdf, the row's current Start [ref]) which states 'Since 1988...has owned and operated' -- but this describes when the corporate entity took its post-reorganization form/name, not when the pipe itself entered service. Great Basin's own official corporate-history page (greatbasingtc.com) is explicit and unambiguous that the physical Main Line was built decades earlier: 'In 1963, Southwest Gas brought gas into northern Nevada by constructing a new natural gas transmission line from the Idaho-Nevada border southwesterly across the northern tier of the State to the Carson City/Reno-Sparks area as well as Lake Tahoe. Along the way, mining and farming communities from Elko to Yerington were converted to natural gas service.' This is a direct, first-person operator statement of original construction and in-service, not a reorganization date. I searched for a second, independent source for the 1963 figure specifically (FERC/Federal Power Commission historical certificate dockets from the 1960s are not digitized/searchable on eLibrary; a general web search was attempted via a DuckDuckGo HTML scrape after the session's WebSearch tool budget was exhausted, but returned no usable results) and did not find one before concluding the search was not cost-effective to continue -- so this fill is single-origin (Great Basin's own site) and capped at medium/independent:false per the tier-discipline rule, despite high confidence in the underlying fact. See the paired Start [ref] fill for the corrected value.
